done_when: A client repo upgrades Forge through one fix whose pull request passes Forge's check

findings.body: The workflow test stops at the install step (`steps[:install + 1]`), and its uv stub records a request without installing Forge. The compatibility case compares `tree` with a copied fingerprint algorithm but never runs v1.1.0's released `forge hook pr-check`; it does not change the pin either. The test can pass without any upgrade pull request passing a real checker. Run the generated job through the check command against an upgrade PR, using the released base checker for the v1.1.0 compatibility case.
findings.title: Not done: tests/test_upgrade_check.py

findings.body: The reported walkthrough records what uv would install, then checks a copied v1.1.0 fingerprint for an ordinary fix. The fix created here does not change `forge.toml`, and the walkthrough never invokes either release's `forge hook pr-check` on an upgrade PR. It therefore skips the covered outcome: an upgrade pull request passing Forge's check.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: The `sed` expression recognizes only an unindented, double-quoted version with no trailing comment, although Forge parses `forge.toml` with `tomllib` (`src/forge/repo.py:205-218`). If a client uses valid single-quoted pins such as `version = 'v1.1.0'` on the base and `version = 'v1.2.0'` on the PR, both `pin` calls return empty. The workflow treats the upgrade as unchanged and installs v1.1.0, so the pinned release's check never runs. Read the version using TOML parsing before comparing it.
findings.title: Read valid TOML versions when selecting the release

why: Upgrading Forge in a client repo is blocked: the upgrade pull request can never pass Forge's check, close calls it clean with stale synced files, and the default branch refuses every command until the upgrade merges
